newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy, Croatia express concern over Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Italy, Croatia express concern over Bosnia.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and his Croatian counterpart Mate Granic expressed concern on Friday over Bosnia, saying the peace accords were not being carried out fully.
Dini's office said in a statement that the ministers had discussed Bonsia as well as Croatia's relations with Italy and the European Union during a "cordial meeting" in Rome.
The statement said the two men "expressed concern over insufficient progress in carrying out the Dayton Accords -- especially the consolidation of common institutions and the reentry of refugees".
Dini also urged "all interested parties" to make sure the accords were respected.

Under the 1995 accords which brought peace to war-ravaged Bosnia, the former Yugoslav republic is supposed to be a single state with two separate entities, one for Serbs and the other a Croat-Moslem federation.

But Bosnia's ethnic factions have resisted integration, many refugees have been prevented from returning home and the inter-ethnic central government has ignored some of the main provisions of the U.S.-brokered treaty.
The statement said that Dini and Granic had also signed a series of bilateral agreements on visas, security and illegal immigration.
